introduction: Khildarak Stronghold holds rumors of lost mines, a cook seeking a steeder egg sack, and a trapped priest offering a bone for kraken proof. Two independent accepted returns have their own cards. Discovery is separate; new journal progress requires active, ready accounting.
orientation: ASK the clan elder about khildarak, hammer or mine. His tale links the lost mines, an enchantress and a bone that unlocks the hammer case. It is a lead for exploration; hearing it does not complete either return.

ASK the young cook about mine, entrance, item or retrieve. Bring one exact steeder egg sack loose for her promised coins and mine-location clue. Matching goods supplied by another player fit her request without a personal hunt.

Egg sacks are declared on the ground in steeder nesting holes. Nest females and other dangers are nearby. Recovering an egg, defeating a creature and the cook accepting an offering are different parts of your journey.

The cook describes a drunken clansdwarf with a circle-eye tattoo, and the elder mentions Clan Spore Seeder. These clues do not yet identify a confirmed responder with a recorded next answer. Follow the stronghold’s conversations and descriptions; the journal does not mark the entrance learned merely from carrying an egg.

ASK the Kuo-Tao priest about bone, journey, kraken or task. He accepts the exact kraken tentacle for an ordinary rib bone. The tentacle is declared on the cavern floor beyond a guarded descent. Accepted proof does not establish who killed the krakens.

The priest’s story describes a route blocked with a rock and the expedition’s hoped-for return home. Shared passage access, moving a guard, your own actions and the party actually reaching home are separate outcomes. His return is accepted independently of the cook’s.

The rib bone fits the hammer’s display case. Recovering the bone, unlocking and opening the shared case, obtaining the hammer, wearing it and receiving one of its effects are distinct events. Owning a reward does not record an unlock or guarantee protection.

Hidden controls, clan halls, shops, training, pets, travel gates and later exchanges add world context. They do not create extra local quest returns. Current-material rows show loose supplies now; accepted history remains after they are spent. Two accepted returns preserve two achievements and two potential dailies, with supply still depending on admitted world stock.
